interpretation: Complete equilibrium occupancy and complete equilibrium source provenance do not exhaust distributional-history state: 45 of the 81 v23 residual aliases differed in their non-source first-arrival maps.
A complete first-arrival map rescued all 45 of those hidden-age residual cases to exact activation-history identity.
First-arrival state itself is still a coarser target than exact activation history: 66/768 design rows remained exact-history unresolved.
Provenance equivalence does not imply colonization-age equivalence; 931 history pairs shared provenance but differed in first-arrival state.
Age memory is not confined to confluence zones. Unique-origin nodes can retain activation-order memory in arrival time even when source identity is structurally fixed.
The final occupied distribution forgot activation history in every row, while first-arrival state differed in 732/768 design rows.
claim_boundary: First-arrival time is structural graph-step time rather than calibrated ecological time.
Colonization-age maps are known-truth state variables, not empirical demographic age.
The 66 residual exact-history aliases are nonidentified only relative to the frozen activation histories and first-arrival target.
No abundance, extinction, persistence or fitness consequence is inferred from age differences in v24.
